entries.13a1073c620f3142: Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd. and 170 domestic and overseas affiliated companies (148 subsidiaries and 22 associates, as of December 31, 2025) make up the group.
entries.15c329e109a95fe3: This business involves machinery used in factories. It manufactures and sells surface mounters that place electronic components on circuit boards, back-end equipment used in semiconductor manufacturing, industrial robots and industrial unmanned helicopters. Surface mounters, back-end semiconductor manufacturing equipment and industrial robots are produced by Yamaha Robotics Co., Ltd. and its overseas subsidiaries in addition to the company itself; industrial unmanned helicopters are produced by the company. Revenue from external customers in the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥111,478 million, segment loss was ¥565 million, and number of employees was 2,718. The company explains that sales of back-end semiconductor manufacturing equipment rose on growing demand for generative AI and advanced packaging, while unit sales of surface mounters and industrial robots fell below the previous year, leaving revenue roughly unchanged; the loss narrowed from ¥3,003 million in the previous year, mainly due to lower manufacturing expenses.
entries.16be10c131360434: Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd. and 170 domestic and overseas affiliated companies (148 subsidiaries and 22 associates, as of December 31, 2025) make up the group. Its head office is located at 2500 Shingai, Iwata, Shizuoka Prefecture. Roles are clearly divided: motorcycles are made by PT.Yamaha Indonesia Motor Manufacturing in Indonesia, India Yamaha Motor Pvt. Ltd. in India, Thai Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd. in Thailand and others, and sales are handled in Japan by Yamaha Motor Sales Co., Ltd. and overseas by sales companies such as Yamaha Motor Corporation, U.S.A. and Yamaha Motor Europe N.V. The number of employees is 55,176. Incidentally, this company is separate from YAMAHA CORPORATION, which makes musical instruments, and was established in July 1955 through a spin-off from Nippon Gakki Seizo K.K. (now YAMAHA CORPORATION). As of December 31, 2025, YAMAHA CORPORATION held 2.98% of issued shares (excluding treasury shares) and was the fourth-largest shareholder.

entries.37acedd63c483b9c: This business involves vehicles that operate on water. It sells outboard motors that propel boats, water vehicles (single- or multi-seat vehicles that run on water), boats, and fishing and Japanese traditional boats. Outboard motors are produced mainly by Yamaha Kumamoto Products Co., Ltd. in addition to the company itself; on January 1, 2026, that company changed its trade name to Yamaha Marine Co., Ltd. Water vehicles are produced by Yamaha Motor Manufacturing Corporation of America in the United States, while boats and fishing and Japanese traditional boats are produced by domestic subsidiaries and subsidiaries in the United States and Europe. Revenue from external customers in the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥527,630 million, and segment profit was ¥53,593 million, the second largest business after Land Mobility. Number of employees: 6,671. The company explains that outboard motor sales were firm in Europe and the Americas but declined mainly in Asia, and demand for water vehicles in the United States, its main market, fell, resulting in lower revenue; profit also declined due to the impact of U.S. tariffs and higher selling, general and administrative expenses.

entries.6b6e799d06dbf8ae: Operating profit for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥126,373 million, down 30.4% from the previous year. The company attributes this to the impact of US tariffs, higher procurement costs, increases in research and development expenses, personnel costs and other selling, general and administrative expenses, and impairment losses of ¥8,876 million on property, plant and equipment in Outdoor Land Vehicles. Profit before tax was ¥133,196 million, and profit attributable to owners of the parent was ¥16,109 million, down 85.1%, reflecting also the reversal of deferred tax assets. By segment profit, Land Mobility (¥108,693 million), Marine (¥53,593 million) and Financial Services (¥21,056 million) were profitable, while Outdoor Land Vehicles (a loss of ¥39,757 million), Other (a loss of ¥16,647 million) and Robotics (a loss of ¥565 million) were loss-making. Losses were not limited to one business; the year clearly separated earning businesses from businesses being restructured.
entries.6d0477b3c99f75e6: This business manufactures and sells land-based vehicles, centered on motorcycles. Besides motorcycles, this segment includes intermediate parts, parts for overseas production, electric power-assisted bicycles and their drive units (e-Kit), electric wheelchairs, automotive engines and automotive components. Motorcycles are produced by the company itself as well as by subsidiaries and affiliates including PT.Yamaha Indonesia Motor Manufacturing, India Yamaha Motor Pvt. Ltd., Thai Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd., Yamaha Motor Vietnam Co., Ltd., Taiwan Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd. and Yamaha Motor da Amazonia Ltda. in Brazil; in Japan they are sold by Yamaha Hatsudoki Hanbai Co., Ltd., and overseas by sales companies including Yamaha Motor Corporation, U.S.A. and Yamaha Motor Europe N.V. Revenue from external customers in the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥1,615,138 million, and segment profit was ¥108,693 million, the largest of the five reportable segments. Number of employees: 39,990. Motorcycle unit sales totaled 4,999,132, of which 4,923,029 were overseas and 3,902,542 were in Asia. The company explains that production and shipments were halted in Vietnam, while sales volumes rose in Indonesia, the Philippines and Thailand, and Japan also grew.

entries.7651ecd264303f43: Revenue for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥2,534,203 million, down 1.6% from the previous year. The company attributes this to the MC business increasing unit sales in Indonesia, the Philippines and Thailand, while production and shipments were halted in Vietnam, and to lower unit sales of water vehicles in the Marine business and of Outdoor Land Vehicles. External customer revenue by reportable segment was Land Mobility ¥1,615,138 million, Marine ¥527,630 million, Outdoor Land Vehicles ¥148,526 million, Financial Services ¥114,033 million, Robotics ¥111,478 million and Other ¥17,395 million.

entries.7ce661234be8a9e4: This business offers sales financing and leasing for people who buy the company’s own products and for dealers. Mainly overseas subsidiaries, including Yamaha Motor Finance Corporation in the United States, provide these services. Revenue from external customers in the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥114,033 million, and segment profit was ¥21,056 million, third in profit after Land Mobility and Marine. Segment assets were ¥892,197 million, the largest of the five reportable segments. Number of employees: 946. The company explains that revenue increased as sales finance receivables grew, while profit declined because interest rate swaps, which had recorded a valuation gain in the previous fiscal year, turned into a valuation loss in the current fiscal year.
entries.7e9875d48f9c8990: A vehicle manufacturer that sells motorcycles and outboard motors worldwide, and also handles four-wheel buggies, industrial robots and sales financing.
entries.866892bee1171d7d: This business, not included in the reportable segments, comprises generators, general-purpose engines, snow blowers and mobility services. Generators, general-purpose engines and snow blowers were sold in Japan through Yamaha Motor Power Products Co., Ltd., and overseas mainly through subsidiaries including Yamaha Motor Corporation, U.S.A. and Yamaha Motor Europe N.V.; however, the company withdrew from the general-purpose engine and generator businesses in December 2025. Revenue from external customers in the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥17,395 million, segment loss was ¥16,647 million, and number of employees was 2,740. The company explains that the loss widened due to costs associated with the transfer of its power products business.

entries.9646ae8be68360c0: This is the business of vehicles used off paved roads. It makes and sells four-wheel buggies, recreational off-highway vehicles (ROV) and golf cars. The United States is the main market; four-wheel buggies and ROVs are made by Yamaha Motor Manufacturing Corporation of America in the United States, and golf cars are made by Yamaha Motor Power Products Co., Ltd. in Japan and by the same US subsidiary overseas. To bring together in 1 the businesses whose main market is the United States, the "Outdoor Land Vehicle Business Operations" was newly established as of January 1, 2025, and from that year it became an independent reportable segment (until then, four-wheel buggies and ROVs were included in "Land Mobility" and golf cars in "Others"). In the fiscal year ended December 2025, revenue from external customers was ¥148,526 million and the segment loss was ¥39,757 million, the largest loss among the 5 reportable segments. An impairment loss on property, plant and equipment of ¥8,876 million was also recorded in this category. The number of employees is 2,111. The company explains that four-wheel buggies were solid, but sales of ROVs and golf cars decreased, and that US tariffs also had an effect.

entries.e1516776687d093c: The largest is motorcycles, with production of 4,966,442 units in the fiscal year ended December 2025. Next are outboard motors, which power boats, at 271,174 units; power-assisted bicycles and drive units (e-Kit) at 338,319 units; water vehicles at 42,078 units; four-wheel buggies and recreational off-highway vehicles at 45,809 units; golf cars at 52,345 units; and surface mounters and industrial robots at 29,166 units. Apart from vehicles, the Robotics products are surface mounters, which place electronic components on circuit boards in factories, and equipment used in the back-end process of semiconductor manufacturing. In its medium-term management plan starting in 2025, the company positions the MC business and the Marine business as core businesses, and Robotics, power-assisted bicycles (SPV) and Outdoor Land Vehicles (OLV) as three strategic businesses.
